questions.prompt: How many molecules are in 0.25 mol of glucose? Give your answer ×10²³ (e.g. type 1.5 for 1.5 × 10²³).
Explain why chemists use moles instead of counting atoms one by one, and why 12 g of carbon and 24 g of magnesium contain the same number of atoms.
questions.modelAnswer: Atoms are far too small and numerous to count individually, so chemists count them by weighing: one mole always contains 6.022 × 10²³ particles, and its mass in grams equals the atomic mass. A magnesium atom (24 u) is twice as heavy as a carbon atom (12 u), so 24 g of magnesium and 12 g of carbon are each one mole and contain the same number of atoms.
rubric: Atoms too small or numerous to count directly
One mole = 6.022 × 10²³ and molar mass = atomic mass in g
Mg atoms twice as heavy, so double the mass gives the same number
questions.explain: Criterion A: explaining the mole concept.
